problem:
Problem description
- There is a finite planning horizon of $$T$$ weeks, indexed by $$t \in \mathcal{T}$$, and a product set $$\mathcal{P}$$, indexed by $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$.
- The factory begins with an initial workforce of $$S_0$$ skilled workers. New workers may be trained, and any worker who completes training becomes a qualified worker with the same production efficiency as a skilled worker.
- Product-specific hourly productivity is given by the vector $$\alpha$$, where $$\alpha_p$$ is the output rate of one qualified worker for product $$p$$.
- Working-time parameters are given by $$h^{\mathrm{reg}}$$ for regular weekly hours and $$h^{\mathrm{ot}}$$ for overtime weekly hours.
- Wage parameters are given by $$w^{\mathrm{sk}}$$ for a skilled worker on regular duty, $$w^{\mathrm{tr}}$$ for a trainee during training, $$w^{\mathrm{post}}$$ for a worker after training, and $$w^{\mathrm{ot}}$$ for an overtime worker.
- Training lasts for $$\tau^{\mathrm{train}}$$ weeks. A trainer can supervise at most $$\rho$$ trainees per training assignment, and during training both the trainer and the trainees are unavailable for production.
- Weekly booked demand is given by the matrix $$D \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{T \times P}$$, where $$D_{t,p}$$ is the demand for product $$p$$ in week $$t$$.
- Delay costs are given by the vector $$\pi$$, where $$\pi_p$$ is the penalty per unit per week of delay for product $$p$$. Any unmet demand may be carried forward and incurs delay penalty until it is delivered.
- The factory must ensure that at least $$N^{\mathrm{req}}$$ new workers have completed training by the end of week $$T$$.
- The planning goal is to choose a workforce-training, overtime, production, and delayed-delivery plan that minimizes total cost over the horizon.

- The required business constraints are:
  - Production in each week must respect the number of workers available for production after excluding workers assigned to training and considering any workers assigned to overtime.
  - A worker assigned to training cannot participate in production during the full training period.
  - Each training assignment must respect the trainer capacity $$\rho$$ and the training duration $$\tau^{\mathrm{train}}$$.
  - The number of workers who complete training by the end of the horizon must be at least $$N^{\mathrm{req}}$$.
  - Demand may be satisfied late, but any unmet quantity must be tracked over time and must accumulate delay penalties until it is delivered.
  - Overtime may only be assigned to eligible qualified workers who are not in training.
  - The plan must determine how many workers are trained, how many workers work overtime, how production is split across products and weeks, and how delayed demand is cleared over time.

- A solution is represented by:
  - $$u_t$$: the number of workers who start training in week $$t$$.
  - $$v_t$$: the number of trainers assigned to training in week $$t$$.
  - $$o_t$$: the number of workers assigned to overtime in week $$t$$.
  - $$q_t$$: the number of workers who complete training by week $$t$$.
  - $$x_{t,p}$$: the quantity of product $$p$$ produced in week $$t$$.
  - $$y_{t,p}$$: the quantity of product $$p$$ delivered in week $$t$$.
  - $$b_{t,p}$$: the backlog or delayed quantity of product $$p$$ remaining at the end of week $$t$$.
  - $$Q_t$$: the number of qualified workers available for production in week $$t$$.
  - $$Z$$: the total cost of the plan.

Input Format
{
  "T": "$$T$$, the number of weeks in the planning horizon",
  "P": "$$P$$, the number of products",
  "product_labels": "List of length $$P$$ identifying the products indexed by $$p \\in \\mathcal{P}$$",
  "demand": "$$D \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{T \\times P}$$, where $$D_{t,p}$$ is the booked demand of product $$p$$ in week $$t$$",
  "initial_workforce": {
    "skilled_workers": "$$S_0$$, the number of skilled workers initially available",
    "already_qualified_workers": "$$Q_0$$, the number of qualified workers already available at the start, if any"
  },
  "productivity": {
    "hourly_output_per_qualified_worker": "$$\\alpha \\in \\mathbb{R}_{>0}^{P}$$, where $$\\alpha_p$$ is the hourly output rate for product $$p$$"
  },
  "working_hours": {
    "regular": "$$h^{\\mathrm{reg}}$$, regular weekly working hours per worker",
    "overtime": "$$h^{\\mathrm{ot}}$$, overtime weekly working hours per overtime worker"
  },
  "wages": {
    "skilled_regular": "$$w^{\\mathrm{sk}}$$, weekly wage of a skilled worker on regular duty",
    "trainee_during_training": "$$w^{\\mathrm{tr}}$$, weekly wage of a trainee during training",
    "post_training": "$$w^{\\mathrm{post}}$$, weekly wage of a worker after training",
    "overtime": "$$w^{\\mathrm{ot}}$$, weekly wage of an overtime worker"
  },
  "training": {
    "duration_weeks": "$$\\tau^{\\mathrm{train}}$$, length of one training assignment in weeks",
    "max_trainees_per_trainer": "$$\\rho$$, maximum number of trainees per trainer per training assignment"
  },
  "delay_penalty": "$$\\pi \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{P}$$, where $$\\pi_p$$ is the delay penalty per unit per week for product $$p$$",
  "required_new_workers_by_horizon": "$$N^{\\mathrm{req}}$$, minimum number of new workers that must complete training by week $$T$$",
  "initial_backlog": "$$B_0 \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{P}$$, initial delayed quantity for each product, if any"
}

Output Format
{
  "weekly_schedule": [
    {
      "week": "$$t$$",
      "training_starts": "$$u_t$$",
      "trainers_assigned": "$$v_t$$",
      "overtime_workers": "$$o_t$$",
      "newly_qualified_workers": "$$q_t$$",
      "production_by_product": "$$x_t \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{P}$$, where the component for product $$p$$ is $$x_{t,p}$$",
      "deliveries_by_product": "$$y_t \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{P}$$, where the component for product $$p$$ is $$y_{t,p}$$",
      "backlog_by_product": "$$b_t \\in \\mathbb{R}_{\\ge 0}^{P}$$, where the component for product $$p$$ is $$b_{t,p}$$",
      "qualified_workers_available": "$$Q_t$$"
    }
  ],
  "total_cost": "$$Z$$"
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "T": 8,
  "P": 2,
  "product_labels": ["I", "II"],
  "demand": [
    [10000, 6000],
    [10000, 7200],
    [12000, 8400],
    [12000, 10800],
    [16000, 10800],
    [16000, 12000],
    [20000, 12000],
    [20000, 12000]
  ],
  "initial_workforce": {
    "skilled_workers": 50,
    "already_qualified_workers": 0
  },
  "productivity": {
    "hourly_output_per_qualified_worker": [10, 6]
  },
  "working_hours": {
    "regular": 40,
    "overtime": 60
  },
  "wages": {
    "skilled_regular": 360,
    "trainee_during_training": 120,
    "post_training": 240,
    "overtime": 540
  },
  "training": {
    "duration_weeks": 2,
    "max_trainees_per_trainer": 3
  },
  "delay_penalty": [0.5, 0.6],
  "required_new_workers_by_horizon": 50,
  "initial_backlog": [0, 0]
}

parameters.name: t_horizon
parameters.description: number of weeks in the planning horizon

parameters.name: initial_qualified_workers
parameters.description: initial number of already qualified workers available at the start

parameters.name: productivity
parameters.description: hourly output rate of one qualified worker for each product

parameters.name: skilled_regular_wage
parameters.description: weekly wage of a skilled worker on regular duty

parameters.name: trainee_wage
parameters.description: weekly wage of a trainee during training

parameters.name: post_training_wage
parameters.description: weekly wage of a worker after training

parameters.name: overtime_wage
parameters.description: weekly wage of an overtime worker

parameters.name: training_duration_weeks
parameters.description: duration of one training assignment in weeks

parameters.name: max_trainees_per_trainer
parameters.description: maximum number of trainees per trainer per training assignment

parameters.name: demand
parameters.description: booked demand of each product in each week

parameters.name: delay_penalty
parameters.description: delay penalty per unit per week for each product

parameters.name: required_completed_trainings
parameters.description: minimum number of workers that must complete training by the end of the horizon

variables.name: training_starts
variables.description: number of workers who start training in each week

variables.name: trainers_assigned
variables.description: number of trainers assigned to training in each week

variables.name: overtime_workers
variables.description: number of workers assigned to overtime in each week

variables.name: newly_qualified_workers
variables.description: number of workers who complete training by each week

variables.name: production_by_product
variables.description: quantity of each product produced in each week

variables.name: deliveries_by_product
variables.description: quantity of each product delivered in each week

variables.name: backlog_by_product
variables.description: backlog of each product remaining at the end of each week

variables.name: qualified_workers_available
variables.description: number of qualified workers available for production in each week

constraints.name: nonnegative_parameters
constraints.description: All demand, penalties, backlog, productivity, hours, wages, training duration, trainer capacity, and workforce input values are nonnegative with the stated positivity requirements.
constraints.formula: D_{t,p}\ge 0\ \forall t\in\mathcal{T},\forall p\in\mathcal{P};\ \pi_p\ge 0\ \forall p\in\mathcal{P};\ B_{0,p}\ge 0\ \forall p\in\mathcal{P};\ S_0\ge 0,\ Q_0\ge 0,\ \alpha_p\ge 0\ \forall p\in\mathcal{P};\ h^{\mathrm{reg}}\ge 0,\ h^{\mathrm{ot}}\ge 0,\ w^{\mathrm{sk}}\ge 0,\ w^{\mathrm{tr}}\ge 0,\ w^{\mathrm{post}}\ge 0,\ w^{\mathrm{ot}}\ge 0,\ \tau^{\mathrm{train}}\ge 0,\ \rho\ge 0,\ N^{\mathrm{req}}\ge 0

constraints.name: decision_variable_nonnegativity
constraints.formula: u_t\ge 0,\ v_t\ge 0,\ o_t\ge 0,\ q_t\ge 0,\ Q_t\ge 0\ \forall t\in\mathcal{T};\ x_{t,p}\ge 0,\ y_{t,p}\ge 0,\ b_{t,p}\ge 0\ \forall t\in\mathcal{T},\forall p\in\mathcal{P}

constraints.name: decision_variable_integrality
constraints.formula: u_t, v_t, o_t, q_t, Q_t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\ \forall t\in\mathcal{T}

constraints.name: production_capacity_limit
constraints.description: Weekly production is limited by available qualified-worker production hours after subtracting trainers and overtime workers.

constraints.name: training_unavailability
constraints.description: Workers assigned to training are unavailable for production for the full training duration, so the number starting training in week t cannot exceed the qualified workers available after accounting for trainers and overtime.

constraints.name: trainer_capacity_limit
constraints.description: Each training assignment must respect the maximum number of trainees per trainer.

constraints.name: training_duration_requirement
constraints.description: Workers who start training in week t complete exactly after the fixed training duration.

constraints.name: minimum_training_completions
constraints.description: At least the required number of workers must complete training by the end of the horizon.

constraints.name: backlog_carryover
constraints.description: Backlog evolves by carrying previous backlog plus current demand minus current deliveries.

constraints.name: backlog_penalty_application
constraints.description: Delayed demand incurs per-unit per-week backlog penalties through the objective via end-of-week backlog levels.

constraints.name: overtime_eligibility
constraints.description: Overtime may only be assigned to eligible qualified workers who are not in training.

constraints.name: planning_decision_scope
constraints.description: The plan must choose training starts, trainers, overtime workers, production, deliveries, and backlog over time.

constraints.name: qualified_worker_balance
constraints.description: Qualified workers available in week t equal the initial workforce plus completed trainings accumulated up to week t minus workers assigned to training and overtime in that week.
constraints.formula: Q_t = Q_0 + \sum_{k=0}^{t} q_k - v_t - o_t\quad \forall t\in\mathcal{T}

constraints.name: backlog_balance
constraints.description: Backlog evolves by carrying previous backlog plus current demand minus current deliveries.
constraints.formula: b_{t,p} = \begin{cases}B_{0,p}+D_{0,p}-y_{0,p} & t=0\\ b_{t-1,p}+D_{t,p}-y_{t,p} & t=1,\dots,T-1\end{cases}\quad \forall t\in\mathcal{T},\forall p\in\mathcal{P}

constraints.name: delivery_backlog_link
constraints.description: Delivered quantity in any week cannot exceed the demand plus beginning backlog available to be satisfied in that week.

constraints.name: nonnegativity_backlog_service
constraints.description: Deliveries cannot exceed the available backlog plus current demand, ensuring backlog remains nonnegative under the balance equation.

constraints.name: workforce_nonnegativity
constraints.description: Workforce-related decision variables are nonnegative integers.

objectives.name: total_cost_minimization
objectives.description: Minimize the total cost over the planning horizon, including workforce, training, overtime, production-related, and backlog delay costs

final_objective.description: Minimize total operational cost over the planning horizon, including regular skilled labor, trainee labor during training, post-training labor, overtime labor, and backlog delay penalties.
